findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com, not Splunkbase, and splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404. The forwarder ships no modular input that polls NVR or camera APIs, so a reader cannot get `nvr:diagnostic` firmware data by 'installing' it. A custom TA or script has to do the polling, and the forwarder only transports the output.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the real collector: a custom scripted or modular input (or HEC push) that queries the VMS/NVR or camera API (ONVIF GetDeviceInformation, Hikvision ISAPI /ISAPI/System/deviceInfo, Milestone) for firmware_version and camera_model, forwarded by a Universal Forwarder or sent over HEC. Drop the 'Splunkbase 617' reference.

findings.explanation: The `implementation` field describes a weekly poll joined to a vendor advisory CSV. The `spl` field runs over earliest=-1d with no lookup, and `description` says it only alerts when fw_variants > 1. None of the fields defines the approved firmware baseline that 'Compliance' in the title implies.
findings.quote: (1) Weekly poll VMS. (2) Join vendor advisory CSV. (3) Maintenance window automation.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `description` and `implementation` describe the same detection: which approved-version lookup (for example, vendor, model and min_approved_fw) is compared, how often, and what makes a camera non-compliant. If the SPL stays drift-only, say so plainly and remove the advisory-join step.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are template text. `model` is a string, so it cannot be 'elevated'. The SPL has no `span=1h`, and a synthetic probe does not create firmware variants. The real causes of false positives are missing.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: staged firmware rollouts, where several versions coexist on purpose during an upgrade; one version reported in different string formats (for example, 'V5.7.3 build 220112' vs '5.7.3'); events with no firmware field counted as an empty-string variant; and hardware revisions sold under one model name that need different firmware.

findings.explanation: `fw_variants` and `model` are computed in the SPL. The raw fields to check are firmware_version or sw_version, camera_model or vendor_model, and vendor. The rest of the field is generic boilerplate (list_inputs RBAC, 24-hour timechart, HTTP 401/429) and does not cover the firmware inventory workflow. It also says earliest=-24h@h while the SPL uses earliest=-1d.
findings.quote: Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`fw_variants, model, vendor`).
findings.suggested_fix: Have the spot-check confirm the raw fields (firmware_version, sw_version, camera_model, vendor_model, vendor) on two known cameras against the VMS inventory. Replace the generic steps with how to build and maintain the approved-firmware lookup. Align the time window with the SPL.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by 'catalog-team', yet it contains template residue, a dead SPL clause and a non-existent Splunkbase ID. No subject-matter expert (SME) could have validated this content.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft or unverified until an SME has reviewed the corrected SPL and the collection path.

findings.explanation: The SPL outputs only vendor, model, a firmware value list and fw_variants. It has no compliance field to chart, and a pie of multivalue firmware lists is not meaningful.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe panels the output supports, such as a table of vendor, model, firmware and fw_variants, plus a count of cameras per firmware version once per-camera rows exist.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `match(fw, "(?i)2018|v1\.0")` runs after `stats`, where `fw` no longer exists because it was aggregated into `firmware`. The 'old firmware' branch can never fire, and the search only reports version drift.

`coalesce(firmware_version, sw_version, "")` counts the empty string as a distinct firmware value, so any model with one event missing the field gets fw_variants=2. `model` falls back to "", which lumps unknown models together. `vendor` is not coalesced, so events without it drop out of `stats ... by vendor model` without notice.

There is no per-camera grain (camera_id, host or IP) and no approved-version lookup. The 'inventory' cannot say which cameras run which firmware, and 'compliance' rests on an arbitrary '2018|v1.0' regex rather than a vendor baseline or advisory list.

summary: The UC is nearly all generated template text. The data-collection story credits the Universal Forwarder with a Splunkbase ID and a modular input it does not have. The implementation promises a vendor-advisory join and maintenance automation that the SPL does not do. Nothing in the text explains what 'compliant' firmware means.
